activity.title: Just finished an incredible week at YC Startup School. First day, I talked to a lot of founders. People nervous about starting something. People 3 months in, grinding through the messy middle. Seed-stage founders learning what it means to actually lead. Then we broke for the Corgi Hackathon and shipped Hacker House in 24 hours with Karthik Paul and Aiden—a social coding space where waiting on your agent becomes community time instead of dead time. Placed 3rd. 🏅 Came back for day two of YC and had more conversations. Same underlying question kept coming up: how do you do this without feeling alone? Then the AWS afterparty. That's where it all synthesized. Smaller conversations. Founders actually opening up about what they're building and what scares them. The hackathon placement is cool. But the clarity, conversation, and experience on what matters when it comes to startups? That's what stays with me. ...more

Had an amazing weekend at Y Combinator startup school! → Met talented builders, many who also just raised their first round (and a couple we’ll be forward deploying Unbrowse to) → Hung out with researchers from Anthropic and OpenAI and learnt how different research is like at a big lab vs startup/academia → Heard from Sam Altman, Jensen Huang , Boris Cherny and Garry Tan on their takes on intelligence in an age of evolving machine intelligence → Had dinner with Charlie Warren where I learnt about his experiences as a partner at YC and where he thinks innovation is headed Glad to meet many other young, ambitious builders and researchers and all the best to everyone!

VCU NSF REU Site Students Showcase Digital Forensics Research at the 26th Annual DFRWS USA Conference—and Earn a Poster Award I am pleased to share that students from the Virginia Commonwealth University NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Site in Digital Forensics attended the 26th Annual Digital Forensics Research Conference (DFRWS USA 2026) in Arlington, Virginia, hosted by George Mason University . The REU students presented posters highlighting the research they conducted during the summer program. The participating students represented institutions across the country: Logan Altomonte — James Madison University Arya Kunisetty — University of California, Los Angeles Sasha Babic — Randolph-Macon College Cosme Boisset — Louisiana State University New Orleans Sebastian Alcibar — Virginia Commonwealth University Emirhan Kir — Rowan University Zoe McIvor — Longwood University Vaishnavi Sharma — Purdue University Sanskriti Gyawali — Virginia Commonwealth University Their projects addressed a broad range of timely digital-forensics and cybersecurity challenges, including PLC security, unmanned aerial systems, point-of-care ultrasound forensics, Starlink network behavior, passive Wi-Fi sensing, cybercrime against older adults, and explainable AI-assisted authorship analysis. Special congratulations to Arya Kunisetty , whose poster, “Forensic Attribution of Human and Autonomous Control in Unmanned Aerial Systems,” received third prize in the poster competition. His work explored whether recovered drone telemetry can distinguish autonomous flight from human control and support the forensic attribution of individual pilots. We also sincerely thank Arya’s mentors, Suramya Pokharel and Eyuphan Bulut , for their guidance, technical support, and commitment to his research. This recognition reflects Arya’s hard work as well as the valuable mentorship that helped shape the project. Congratulations to all the REU students for their hard work, professionalism, and excellent presentations. I am deeply grateful to the faculty members, postdoctoral researchers, graduate-student mentors, and collaborators who helped the students develop their research ideas, conduct rigorous experiments, prepare their posters, and confidently present their work. I am also grateful to Dr. Kemal Akkaya , Chair of the Department of Computer Science, and the VCU College of Engineering administration, including Dean Azim Eskandarian , Senior Associate Dean Gary Tepper , and Associate Dean for Research and Innovation Susan Barker , for their continued support of undergraduate research, faculty mentorship, and the NSF REU program. It was especially rewarding to see undergraduate researchers from multiple institutions engage with the international digital-forensics community, receive constructive feedback, and build connections that will support their future academic and professional development. This work was supported by the National Science Foundation (NSF) .

I’ve been building Churnary AI with my co-founders Riyan Anosh , Aditya Kolekar , and Pranjal Mishra for a while, and I’m excited to finally share where we are today. What started as a hackathon idea has grown into something we believe can make a real difference for local businesses. Most businesses do not lose customers all at once. It happens quietly, one missed visit, purchase, or appointment at a time. Churnary AI is a customer retention platform that helps local businesses: → Identify customers who may be at risk of leaving → Understand how and why customer behavior has changed → See how much revenue may be at risk → Create personalized win-back emails using customer history → Approve campaigns manually or automate them → Track the customers and revenue they recover Businesses can connect Square or Stripe, or simply upload a CSV. There is no complicated CRM or technical setup required. Our goal is simple: help businesses reconnect with loyal customers before they are gone. We are currently adding new features and preparing to pilot Churnary AI with local businesses. If you own a business or know someone who may be interested in trying it, we would love to connect. Which Churnary AI feature would be most useful to your business? Explore the platform: https://churnary.ai/ As always, we’re incredibly grateful to everyone who has shared their advice and guidance along the way. As first-time founders, having people willing to support us, challenge us, and help us grow truly makes all the difference. #CustomerRetention #SmallBusiness #BusinessGrowth #SaaS

1st place at a hackathon was the start. The real test came after. At the Super Solo Agent Skills Hack Day, my team and I built social-content-autopilot, a Claude Agent Skill that turns one piece of verified product info into native posts for Instagram, LinkedIn, and X, complete with a creative brief and a measurement plan. Built for real reach, not fake virality. But winning a hackathon just means the judges liked it. The question we actually cared about: will real people use it? So we put it on the Botlearn Skill Hunt as a 7-day challenge to find out how many people would pick it up and run with it and we took 1st place there too. Check out the leaderboard: https://lnkd.in/gfhUf5-g Built with Asim Siddiqui , Riyan Anosh , and Aditya Kolekar . Thanks to the organizers, sponsors, and judges, including co-hosts Botlearn｜Aibrary and Inference.ai . #BotLearn #AIAgents

Last week in SF I had the pleasure of helping organize the RocketRide Cloud launch event! During the event, I got to give an on-stage demo of a project I built entirely as a RocketRide pipeline: a video translator. The pipeline allows you to upload videos in any language (such as YouTube videos or TikToks), it detects the source language, and transcribes it to English. The repo: https://lnkd.in/gpBqmZaP

Spent the weekend at the Y Combinator Hackathon building BountyHunters 🤠 , a tool that helps insurance agents find the households most likely to need them. The angle I liked: most "synthetic persona" tools model individual people. We built at the household level instead, grounded entirely in real public data, SF property records and permits, joined and validated, with every signal traceable to an actual data point. Then we made it interactive: an insurance agent can talk to a household, grounded in that property's real data, to practice a pitch or pull the context for a real one. It placed top 5. I'm an ML/AI engineer (real-data pipelines, ML systems, inference optimization), building all summer. If you're working on something technical in ML/AI and want a collaborator, reach out. Built with Zhi Hao Teo , Gulnoza U and Saahith Veeramaneni .
